trigger.summary: The four named provider HTTP clients are registered with a bare AddHttpClient(name) in ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.RegisterProviderHttpClients and therefore inherit the .NET default AllowAutoRedirect=true. SecretLease.ApplyTo adds the X-Api-Key header to the shared HttpRequestMessage, and a redirect hop clones that request, so the credential is re-sent to whatever origin the 3xx Location names. Reproduced end to end against the exact DI shape ArrTagsServiceRegistrator builds. This widens the credential's egress beyond the configured connection, contrary to ADR-005's requirement that the key is added to the current request only and confined to the outbound authenticated request while it is being sent. MEDIUM rather than HIGH because the configured base URL is administrator-supplied and the redirect must come from that configured provider or from a network position that can already read the key; it is not remotely triggerable by an unauthenticated third party against the Jellyfin host.
trigger.user_decision: Fix it now and re-verify, rather than accept it as a shipped limitation. The user decision is the authority for this corrective chain; no new decision gate was opened, because the required behavior (the key never leaves the configured connection) is already stated by accepted ADR-005 and the remedy is a transport configuration on the plugin's own named clients, which docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 2.4 already prescribes.
trigger.consequence: The fix changes ArrTags.dll, so it invalidates the 1.2.0.0 artifact identity recorded by task 21.3 (619,538 bytes; SHA-256 505804992a50d7aa073b07cfaa8dc0c8ac9a95041a7c394d8bd54dd959f90762; MD5 3100aae94a2b4aedf222eca040675271; 7 entries; per-entry hashes; manifest.json checksum; docs/release/build-and-release.md) and the live pinned-host matrix recorded by task 21.4, which was run against the superseded artifact. The release security review must be re-run against the corrected candidate before task 21.6 tags v1.2.0.

tasks.objective: Make it impossible for the plugin to send the X-Api-Key header to any origin other than the configured provider connection, by configuring every named Arr HTTP client not to follow redirects, and prove the property with a transport test that reproduces the reviewer's scenario.

dependencies: 21.5 (the finding, its reproduction, and the evidence of the current registration shape)
work: In src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs RegisterProviderHttpClients, set the primary handler of all four named clients (ArrHttpClientNames.Sonarr, ArrHttpClientNames.Radarr, and the two .Insecure names) to a handler with AllowAutoRedirect=false, or otherwise configure MaxAutomaticRedirections=0, and set the same on the existing CreateInsecureHandler so the opt-in TLS relaxation does not also change credential scope. Keep handler pooling and the existing DI shape; do not add a dependency.

Decide and record how a 3xx response is now surfaced. A not-followed redirect must fail closed as a bounded provider error through the existing ArrProviderError path (bounded code, no response body, header, or Location value, no secret), consistent with the existing ClassifyStatus behavior for non-success statuses. Do not introduce a new unbounded-work or retry path: the bounded retry count and backoff must be unchanged.

Add a transport test in tests/ArrTags.Tests that stands up two local origins (a provider origin answering 302 with a Location naming a second origin, and the second origin) and asserts that the second origin receives no request carrying the key, for the client shape the plugin registers. Cover the strict and the insecure-TLS client of at least one provider, and assert the registration itself pins the behavior (so a future re-registration that drops the setting fails the test rather than silently restoring the leak).

Record the transport constraint where the architecture documents the provider client boundary (docs/architecture/07-sonarr-and-radarr-integration.md and, if it carries the secret-transport clauses, docs/architecture/11-failure-consistency-and-security-policy.md) and, per the reviewer's recommended action, record the decision in ADR-005 or as an explicit implementation note against ADR-005. ADR-005 is an accepted decision record; amending it is an architecture change and needs the smallest explicit decision. If the worker concludes the existing ADR-005 text already authorizes the behavior and only needs an implementation note, that is sufficient and must be stated in the report.
Update docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md with the security-relevant behavior change.

tests.level: integration (transport, against the real registration shape) plus unit coverage of the 3xx classification
required: A test that fails on the pre-fix code: with AllowAutoRedirect left at the .NET default, the second origin receives the X-Api-Key; with the fix, it receives nothing. The test must be written so that reverting the fix fails it (the reviewer reproduced the pre-fix behavior, so the scenario is known to be discriminating).
A test asserting the four named clients are all registered with redirect-following disabled, so the two insecure-TLS names cannot regress independently.
A test asserting a not-followed 3xx surfaces as a bounded provider error with no secret, no Location value, and no response body, and that the retry count stays within the configured bound.
verification_surfaces: The default suite and the host-guarded suite pass with no new failures.

Renderer goldens and byte-determinism are unaffected: the change is transport-only and must not alter any committed golden, so the golden oracle must still pass unchanged. If a golden changes, that is a defect, not an expected consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Given a provider origin that answers 302 with a Location naming a different origin, the plugin issues no request to that other origin, and the X-Api-Key value is never sent to it.

All four named provider clients (strict Sonarr, strict Radarr, and both opt-in insecure-TLS clients) are registered with redirect-following disabled; a registration that drops the setting fails a test.
The opt-in insecure-TLS relaxation still works for its intended purpose and does not re-enable redirect-following or change the header the plugin sends.
A not-followed 3xx surfaces as a bounded provider error containing no secret, no response body, no header value, and no Location value, and the configured retry bound is unchanged.
A test exists that demonstrably fails on the pre-fix registration (the report records the pre-fix failure and the post-fix pass).
No committed renderer golden changes and no RenderVersion or renderer-configuration schema bump is introduced; the change is transport-only.

The transport constraint is recorded in the provider-integration architecture documentation and as an implementation note against ADR-005, and the ADR-005 decisions index row is updated only if an ADR was actually amended.
scripts/check-docs.sh passes and the default and host-guarded suites pass.

decision_gates.note: The connection defaults and supported provider ranges are unaffected; the fix constrains transport only and does not retune a configurable default.

The required behavior is already stated by accepted ADR-005 (the key is added to the current request only and is confined to the outbound authenticated request while it is being sent). The remedy is a transport configuration on the plugin's own named clients, already prescribed by docs/research/jellyfin-12-architecture.md section 2.4. If the worker or reviewer judges that honoring a legitimate provider redirect requires a new policy, that is a new decision and the task stops at the decision boundary rather than implementing it.

risks: A provider or reverse proxy in front of it that legitimately issues a 3xx (for example a trailing-slash or http-to-https redirect) would now fail closed as a provider error instead of being followed. This is the intended behavior and is surfaced as a bounded error, not silently swallowed; it is called out in the changelog and the architecture documentation so an operator can diagnose it.
The insecure-TLS clients use a separate handler; fixing only the two strict names would leave the leak on the opt-in path. The registration test must cover all four names.
The retry loop re-sends on transient failures; a redirect must not be treated as a transient retryable status or it would multiply requests. The classification must be checked, not assumed.

decision_gates.note: The fix constrains provider transport. It introduces no configuration, no setting, and no user-visible toggle, so it does not reopen DG-6 (defaults) or DG-9 (provider ranges), and it does not require path-mapping scope (DG-5). If the implementation turns out to need a configurable redirect policy, that is a new decision and is out of scope for this chain.

ADR-005 already requires the API key to be added to the current request only and confined to the outbound authenticated request while it is being sent, and forbids query-string authentication. Disabling redirect-following implements that decision rather than changing it. An explicit ADR-005 amendment is only required if the worker or reviewer concludes the existing text does not authorize the behavior; ADR-005 is an accepted decision record, so any amendment is the smallest explicit decision and is recorded before it is relied on.

open_questions: USER DECISION APPLIED (not open): fix SEC-21.5-01 now and re-verify, rather than accept it as a shipped limitation. That decision is the authority for tasks 21.7-21.10 and for re-ordering 21.6 last.

CONFIRM (not a blocker): whether honoring a legitimate provider redirect is ever required. The corrective chain assumes it is not (the read paths are fixed GETs against the configured base URL, and a redirect is not a documented Arr API behavior). If an operator legitimately depends on a redirect, the correct outcome is a bounded provider error they can diagnose, not silent credential forwarding. Adding a configurable redirect policy would be a new decision and is out of scope.

CONFIRM (not a blocker): whether SEC-21.5-01's disposition also warrants a documentation note in the accepted plan (docs/planning/v1.2.md) or is satisfied by the ADR-005 implementation note plus the release documentation. The accepted plan document is not rewritten; the mapping of the corrective chain to Phase 21 is recorded in PLANS.md and in this record.

Every phase acceptance criterion added by this change has a single owning task, and no decision gate is left unowned: the only candidate gate (whether an ADR-005 amendment is needed) is resolved as 'not required unless the implementation shows otherwise', with the stop-at-the-boundary rule recorded in 21.7 and 21.10.

The corrected candidates' evidence lives in the 21.8/21.9/21.10 report directories rather than in the 21.3/21.4/21.5 ones, because docs/implementation/** is immutable history and check-agents.sh keys the per-task report pairing by task id. The superseded reports remain the record of the first candidate and are cited by the new reports.
